content: {"summary":"During the 22 May 2025 login slowdown auth‑service emitted 503 responses itself, not forwarding errors from auth‑db. The service’s pgx connection pool became exhausted, causing new logins to wait; once the number of in‑flight logins per pod exceeded the internal ceiling of 64, auth‑service returned 503 immediately.","likely_cause":"Exhaustion of auth‑service’s pgx connection pool caused the per‑pod concurrent‑login limit (64) to be exceeded, triggering auth‑service’s built‑in 503 response.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The 503 is generated by auth‑service itself, not forwarded from auth‑db","evidence_ids":["INC-0046#1"],"quote":"The `503` is auth-service's own doing."},{"text":"Auth‑service returns 503 when more than 64 logins per pod are in flight","evidence_ids":["INC-0046#1"],"quote":"once more than 64 logins per pod are in flight at the same time, it returns `503` straight away"},{"text":"New logins found the connection pool empty and waited behind in‑progress logins","evidence_ids":["INC-0046#0"],"quote":"New logins found the pool empty and waited behind the ones in progress"},{"text":"The shortage causing the issue was inside auth‑service, not auth‑db","evidence_ids":["INC-0046#0"],"quote":"The shortage was inside the service."}],"next_checks":["Collect pgx pool occupancy metrics for each auth‑service pod during the incident period","Confirm the configured per‑pod concurrent‑login ceiling (64) in the auth‑service deployment configuration","Correlate timestamps of pool exhaustion with the first observed 503 responses","Check for recent changes to pool size or concurrency limits that could affect behavior"]}
